g.text: A cabin layout is not "how many seats fit". The number is what the exits allow.
Each pair of exits carries a number, and the seats are the sum: 45 + 35 + 45 = 125 here.
Add a row and the drawing stays legal only while that sum does.
At the Type III the rule is about the passage, not the seat - so the seatbacks cannot recline.
The aircraft, the cabin and the seat count are fictional.
SEATS PER PAIR OF EXITS (14 CFR 25.807)
SO THE SEAT COUNT IS A SUM
exit row - wider, and the seatbacks do not recline
the floor is not what limits it
unobstructed for at least the width
of the narrowest seat on board
count in their most adverse position
